data.narrative:
Fossa Systems is a Series A-stage space & aerospace company that has raised €6.3M to date. The valuation assessment draws on a comparable universe of three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private peers (Cowboy Space Corporation, Aalyria, and Starcloud) and five public Space & Aerospace companies (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL).

Two valuation methods proved applicable. The stage-progression approach, using the €6.3M total raised as a proxy base and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A advancement, implies a valuation of €13M. The peer-median method applied the median valuation of three comparable private companies in the same sector and stage, yielding €1.3B. The peer valuations range from €1.1B to €2.0B. Public-comp anchoring using the sector's 25.3x median price-to-sales multiple could not be applied due to the absence of disclosed revenue figures.

These two methods triangulate to a valuation range of €11M (low), €656M (median), and €1.5B (high). The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty around the appropriate comp set weighting—specifically, whether near-stage private peers or later-stage public proxies should dominate the analysis. Revenue traction, customer concentration, and competitive positioning relative to peers remain critical but unspecified variables that would narrow this range.
